transcript: So this is a story of how I ended up arriving the subway with three time Tony Award winner and all around theater legend Patti Lapone. The year is 2019, it is early may, and I am in the 59th Street subway station. I am minding my own business like I typically do in subway stations. I have my headphones in, head down on my phone, don't really want to be bothered. And the best way I can describe it, and this is going to sound like a lie, but I swear it's true, is I felt the energy in the subway station shift. Like, I just instantly felt a presence enter the subway station. And so I turn around and immediately I spot Patti Lapone like 30 feet away from me. So this point I start freaking out. I'm like, what do I do? That's Patti Lapone. Like, do I go up to say hi? Hi. Do I let her just be? Cause she's with a friend having conversation. I didn't want to interrupt. But ultimately I decide it's Patti Lapone. I may literally never have this opportunity again. I have to go up and say something. So I go up to her, I'm like, hi, I'm really sorry to bother you. I just want to say I'm a really big fan. Would you mind if I get a picture with you? And at that point, the train was like a minute away. So she's like, yeah, you can Get a picture, but you better make it fast, because the train's gonna be here. And then she poses with her friend as if to say, take a picture of us. So I do, because I'm not gonna say no to Patti Lapone. And if she doesn't wanna get a picture with me, that's fine. I'm not gonna push. Uh, she was very kind. Um, but then after I take this photo, her friend says, would you like me to get a photo of the two of you? And at that point, I'm like, oh, yes. What a great idea you just had. That totally wasn't my initial intention. Uh, that would be really great. Thank you very much. So this point, the train is coming into the station, and Patty's like, yes, okay, we can get a picture together, but let's get on the train first, uh, so we don't miss it. And so here we are on the subway together. Her friend very graciously takes the photo for us. And I once again say, thank you so much. I am a really big fan. Again, barely able to produce any kind of coherent words. Uh, but she was very, very, very sweet. And after we took the photo, I then went and sat in, like, another section of the train so as to not bother her for the rest of the train ride. But that's not where the story ends, because I am now in the section over I am, like, texting everyone I know, being like, you will never believe who I just met on the subway. But the stop that Patty was getting off at comes, and instead of exiting through the door that we came through, she crosses towards me and exits the door across from me. And as she's leaving, she looks at me and she says, bye, sweetie. And it is in that moment that I just melt into a puddle onto the floor of the Uptown C train. Uh, and I'm pretty sure there's still a piece of me there to this day.
classificationReason: Personal anecdote about meeting Patti LuPone in subway station in 2019 - not a review of any specific stage production
